US-119-HR10935.title: Stockdale Mountain Land Conveyance Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10935.description: To direct the Secretary of the Interior to offer for sale certain Bureau of Land Management land in Monterey County, California, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10935.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Interior Department to offer about 2,000 acres of Bureau of Land Management land in Monterey County, California, for public sale within 2 years after it becomes law. The land would be sold by competitive bidding for at least fair market value, and the sale would follow existing federal land sale rules. Money from the sale would fund grants for wildlife habitat protection, habitat restoration, and related conservation work for state, local, and nonprofit groups, with priority for Stockdale Mountain and southern Monterey County.

US-119-HR10913.title: Eliminating Dangerous Preservatives Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10913.description: To amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to make adulterated food containing certain preservatives, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10913.aiSummary: The bill would change food safety law so food for people that contains any amount of butylated hydroxyanisole, butylated hydroxytoluene, or tert-butylhydroquinone would count as adulterated, meaning not meeting the law’s food standard. It would apply to food put into interstate commerce 2 years after enactment. The Food and Drug Administration would have to write rules within 2 years, and the Health and Human Services secretary would have to send Congress a report within 3 years.

US-119-HR10858.title: CARE for Blood Cancer Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10858.description: To establish the National Blood Cancer Program, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10858.aiSummary: The bill would create a National Blood Cancer Program at the Health and Human Services Department. It would fund grants for state, local, tribal, and other groups to raise awareness, train health workers, and help people with blood cancer and their caregivers. It would also fund colleges and medical centers to study better tests and treatments, and it would require yearly reports to Congress.

US-119-HR837.title: To require the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County, Arizona.
US-119-HR837.summary:
This bill directs the Forest Service to convey specified property to Gila County, Arizona, upon the county's submission of a written request for such conveyance. The property, identified as the Gila County Area, consists of approximately 232.9 acres of National Forest System land located in the Tonto National Forest in Arizona.

The county must use the land for the purposes of serving and supporting veterans. If any land conveyed under this bill ceases to be used for such purpose, all right, title, and interest in and to the land shall revert to the United States, at the discretion of the Forest Service.

The conveyance must be made with a quitclaim deed and without consideration (value, such as payment, provided in exchange for the property).

The Forest Service must not be required to provide any covenant or warranty for the land and improvements conveyed to the county under such conveyance.

As a condition of the conveyance, the county must pay all the costs associated with the conveyance, including any (1) surveys, (2) environmental analysis or resource survey required under federal law, and (3) analysis required to comply with certain provisions of the National Historic Preservation Act.
US-119-HR837.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-01-31)

US-119-HR10814.title: REAL Political Advertisements Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10814.description: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10814.aiSummary: The bill would require political ads that use generative AI images or video to include a clear notice saying so. It would also expand federal election ad rules to cover some paid online ads and set rules for large online platforms and ad vendors. The changes would apply to communications made on or after January 1, 2027, and the Federal Election Commission would have to report to Congress every two years after the law takes effect.

US-119-HR10759.title: Tariff Relief for American Development and Employment Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

US-119-HR10759.description: To establish a tariff-funded program to protect United States manufacturers, workers, farmers, and supply chains from disproportionate economic harm resulting from tariffs and foreign retaliatory measures, to encourage domestic investment and reshoring, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10759.aiSummary: This bill would create a tariff-funded aid program for U.S. manufacturers, farmers, workers, and supply chains that are hurt by tariffs and foreign retaliation. It would offer refundable tax credits, low-interest loans, investment credits, and emergency bridge financing to help with domestic production, jobs, training, and supply chain changes. People or businesses seeking aid would need to show real tariff-related harm and agree to keep the supported work in the United States.

US-119-S1055.title: Indian Health Service Emergency Claims Parity Act
US-119-S1055.summary:
Indian Health Service Emergency Claims Parity Act

This bill extends from 72 hours to 15 days the time period to notify the Purchased/Referred Care (PRC) program of emergency medical care received from a non-Indian Health Service (IHS) medical provider or at a non-IHS medical facility. This bill does not apply to individuals who are elderly or disabled, who continue to have a 30-day notification requirement for emergency services.

The IHS provides medical and dental services directly to American Indian and Alaska Native patients whenever possible. The PRC program pays for medical or dental care that is provided away from an IHS or tribal health care facility. The PRC program must be notified of requests for authorization of payment for health care services from a non-IHS provider.

Currently in emergency cases, the patient, an individual on behalf of the patient, or the medical care provider must, within 72 hours after the beginning of treatment for the condition or after admission to a health care facility, notify a PRC authorizing official of the need for the emergency medical care. This bill instead allows the patient, other individual, or provider to notify PRC within 15 days of the treatment or admission.
US-119-S1055.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in Senate, 2025-03-13)

US-119-S5653.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
US-119-S5653.summary:
Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026

This bill modifies federal permitting processes, including environmental reviews, to expedite a wide range of projects.

The bill limits the scope of the National Environmental Policy Act and expedites environmental reviews, including by
• further limiting the types of federal actions that trigger environmental review,
• narrowing the range of alternatives that must be considered in environmental reviews, and
• exempting additional types of projects from environmental review.

It also establishes deadlines for issuing permits once an environmental review is complete.

The bill also limits permit obligations under the Clean Water Act, including by
• narrowing the scope of review for water quality certifications,
• extending the term for permits issued under the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System, and
• limiting the time period for review of permits for discharges of dredged or fill materials.

It also modifies requirements concerning threatened or endangered species to expedite the review of federal permits, including by shortening the timeline for certain consultations.

Additionally, the bill addresses numerous aspects of energy infrastructure permitting, including by
• expanding the authority of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to issue construction permits for certain interstate electricity transmission projects;
• directing FERC to establish ratepayer protections related to certain large computational loads (e.g. data centers);
• removing permit requirements for onshore oil and gas drilling on nonfederal land; and
• accelerating renewable energy, geothermal, hydropower, or offshore energy projects.

It also limits the scope of the National Historic Preservation Act, including by limiting what types of projects trigger review.
US-119-S5653.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in Senate, 2026-09-30)

US-119-S5653.aiSummary: This bill would speed up federal permits and environmental reviews for many kinds of projects. It would narrow when reviews are needed under the National Environmental Policy Act, limit some water and historic review rules, and shorten some endangered species checks. It would also affect energy projects, oil and gas drilling on nonfederal land, and large power users like data centers.

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5576.description: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5576.aiSummary: The bill would create the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board within the Commerce Department to address risks from artificial intelligence. It would include federal officials and outside experts, and it would set rules for meetings, member terms, classified information, and conflict-of-interest checks. It also says the board could work with foreign partners on testing, guidance, information sharing, and common evaluation methods for advanced AI systems.

US-119-S5554.title: Ovarian Cancer IMPACT Act
committees: Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5554.description: A bill to modernize and strengthen Federal efforts to improve ovarian cancer awareness, hereditary cancer risk assessment, access to genetic counseling and testing, and access to specialty care, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5554.aiSummary: The bill would expand federal work on ovarian cancer awareness, genetic risk checks, genetic counseling and testing, and access to specialty care. It would require many health plans to cover certain genetic testing, early detection, and risk-reducing care for people with ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer, or a strong family history of hereditary cancer. It would also create grant programs for outreach and rural care, and it sets aside $20 million a year for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for some of these efforts.

US-119-HR10418.title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act

US-119-HR10418.description: To require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to establish, build, and operate a technology platform to modernize the disability claims process in accordance with the plan submitted by the Secretary under the Honoring our PACT Act of 2022 for the modernization of information technology systems of the Veterans Benefits Administration, and for other purposes.

It would set rules for using automation and artificial intelligence, including human review and final decisions by VA staff, and it would require data sharing across VA health, benefits, and Defense systems. US-119-HR9902.aiSummary: The bill would stop federal buildings, facilities, and programs from being named after living elected officials or political appointees for a set time after they leave office. US-119-HR9407.description: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to establish the small distiller domestic sourcing credit.
US-119-HR9407.aiSummary: The bill would create a new tax credit for small distillers who use mostly U.S.-grown materials. The change would apply to spirits produced after December 31, 2025.

US-119-S4465.title: A bill to amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
US-119-S4465.summary:
This act extends the authorities of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) until June 12, 2026.

Title VII of FISA generally addresses electronic surveillance and other methods of acquiring foreign intelligence information that are directed at targets outside the United States. Title VII includes surveillance under Section 702, which concerns acquiring communications of non-U.S. persons believed to be outside the United States to obtain foreign intelligence information. Information about U.S. persons may incidentally be acquired by this type of surveillance and subsequently queried (searched) under certain circumstances.

For additional information see
• CRS In Focus, IF11451 Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) ; and
• CRS Report, R48592 FISA Section 702 and the 2024 Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act .
